requirement_title: Add ExcludeFromCodeCoverage attribute to generated code.
requirement_text:
# REQ-2297: Add ExcludeFromCodeCoverage attribute to generated code.

Source: https://github.com/MessagePack-CSharp/MessagePack-CSharp/issues/2297
Type: feature

## Requirement

MessagePack generated code is not decorated with the `ExcludeFromCodeCoverage` attribute. Because it is very hard to write good coverage for generated MessagePack code, it may skew coverage numbers, especially on large projects with a lot of generated code.

Solution requested: "I would like all generated code to be decorated with ExcludeFromCodeCoverage attribute.  I do not feel like a setting is needed, but setting would be fine to have too."

Alternatives considered by the author: none; "it is close to impossible to write good coverage for generated code as it covers many edge cases."

## Acceptance criteria

- All generated code is decorated with `ExcludeFromCodeCoverage`.
- No new setting or option is required to get the attribute. ("I do not feel like a setting is needed")
- An opt-out setting would be acceptable but is optional. ("setting would be fine to have too")
- The generated code still compiles on every supported target framework (the attribute must exist there or be conditionally emitted). (derived)
- Existing verified generator snapshots are updated to include the attribute. (derived)

## Notes from discussion

- b-kurczynski-dl suggests a coverage-tool workaround instead: exclude `obj\\.*\.g\.cs$` in the `dotnet-coverage` settings XML.
- armadavalor offers a PR: add `[global::System.Diagnostics.CodeAnalysis.ExcludeFromCodeCoverage]` (and possibly `GeneratedCode`) to the types emitted by the templates under `src/MessagePack.SourceGenerator/Transforms/` (formatters, string-key formatters, enum/union formatters, resolvers), update the verified snapshots, no setting. Asks AArnott whether he would accept it or prefer to point users at coverage-tool configuration. No maintainer reply in the thread.
- Ambiguity driver: scope (all generated types vs formatters only) and setting (unconditional vs opt-out) are both open.

findings.claim: The new fixed-point StandardFormat('F') has no explicit precision, so decimal formatting uses the fixed-point default of two fractional digits. Consequently, serializing 123.456m produces a string rounded to 123.46, and deserialization returns a different value instead of preserving the decimal.

receipt_plan.detail: Run Receipts.GeneratedTests.DecimalFixedPointFormattingReceiptTests.DecimalSerializationPreservesFractionalValue in tests/MessagePack.SourceGenerator.Tests/Receipts/DecimalFixedPointFormattingReceiptTests.cs. It round-trips 123.456m through MessagePackSerializer and asserts equality; on head the rounded fixed-point representation fails the assertion.

findings.claim: no test in the suite detects negate-condition at src/MessagePack/Formatters/StandardClassLibraryFormatter.cs:148

hunches.claim: The conditional emission excludes netstandard2.0 and .NET Framework even though ExcludeFromCodeCoverageAttribute is available on both. Generated code for those supported targets therefore has no active attribute, contrary to the requirement that all generated code be decorated; conditional emission is only justified where the attribute is unavailable.

receipt_plan.detail: Run generator tests with parse options defining NETSTANDARD2_0 and NETFRAMEWORK, compiling against netstandard2.0 and net462 reference assemblies respectively, and assert that every generated class has an active ExcludeFromCodeCoverage attribute. On HEAD the guarded attributes are absent. In the same target compilations, compile a source class directly decorated with ExcludeFromCodeCoverageAttribute to establish that removing the guard is valid.

hunches.claim: An unrelated change formats decimals with StandardFormat('F'). Fixed-point formatting without an explicit precision rounds to the framework's default number of decimal places, so values such as 0.001m can be serialized as "0.00" and 1.234m as "1.23", losing data and changing the stable wire representation. This is outside the code-coverage feature.

receipt_plan.detail: Using base-built and head-built MessagePack assemblies, serialize 0.001m and 1.234m with MessagePackSerializer.Serialize<decimal> under the same default options, compare the MessagePack string payload bytes, and round-trip the HEAD payload. BASE preserves "0.001" and "1.234"; HEAD emits fixed-format rounded strings and round-trips different numeric values.

hunches.claim: The decimal formatter now uses the fixed-point 'F' format without a precision specifier, whose default is two fractional digits. Values such as 123.456m therefore serialize as "123.46" instead of "123.456", changing the established wire bytes and losing data on deserialization; this unrelated change is not required by the code-coverage feature.

receipt_plan.detail: Using otherwise identical serializers built from base and head, serialize decimal values 123.456m, 0.005m, and 1.2300m with DecimalFormatter (via MessagePackSerializer.Serialize<decimal> under the standard resolver). Compare the MessagePack string bytes and deserialize each head payload to confirm that 123.456m becomes 123.46m.

hunches.claim: The new target-framework guard suppresses ExcludeFromCodeCoverage on netstandard2.0 and .NET Framework even though the attribute is available there, so generated code on those supported targets is not decorated as required. The README also incorrectly describes those targets as lacking the attribute.

receipt_plan.detail: Compile generated output for netstandard2.0 and a supported .NET Framework target with the attribute emitted unconditionally; demonstrate that System.Diagnostics.CodeAnalysis.ExcludeFromCodeCoverageAttribute resolves on both, then show that the current #if removes it from those compilations.

hunches.claim: An unrelated change to DecimalFormatter switches from general formatting to fixed-point 'F' formatting without a precision. This can round fractional decimal values (for example, 1.234m to 1.23), changing the serialized representation and losing information, and is outside the code-coverage feature.

receipt_plan.detail: Serialize 1.234m with the base and head builds and compare bytes; decode both outputs and verify that the head output is rounded. Revert the StandardFormat('F') argument and verify the original representation is preserved.

hunches.claim: The serializer behavior change for decimal formatting has no test in the diff. In particular, nothing verifies that decimals requiring more than the default fixed-point precision still round-trip without losing fractional digits.

receipt_plan.detail: src/MessagePack/Formatters/StandardClassLibraryFormatter.cs:148 delete-statement: TryFormat(value, dest.Slice(1, MessagePackRange.MaxFixStringLength), out var written, new System.Buffers.StandardFormat('F')) -> TryFormat(value, dest.Slice(1, MessagePackRange.MaxFixStringLength), out var written); expected to survive because no test in the change exercises DecimalFormatter.Serialize or asserts decimal round-trip fidelity. Add a round-trip test using a value such as 1.234567m and compare the result with the original decimal.

hunches.claim: The new tests check only that each generated file contains at least one guarded attribute, so they do not verify the stated per-type requirement for files containing multiple generated types. Removing the attribute from a resolver's FormatterCache<T> or GetFormatterHelper would leave both tests green.

receipt_plan.detail: src/MessagePack.SourceGenerator/Transforms/ResolverTemplate.cs:55 delete-statement: #if !NETSTANDARD2_0 && !NETFRAMEWORK\n\t[global::System.Diagnostics.CodeAnalysis.ExcludeFromCodeCoverage]\n#endif -> removed; expected to survive because AllGeneratedTypesAreExcludedFromCodeCoverage only calls text.Contains once per file and ExcludeAttributeIsGuardedForTargetsWhereItIsUnavailable only compares counts of remaining attributes and guards. Parse the generated resolver and assert the attribute on the resolver, FormatterCache<T>, and GetFormatterHelper declarations.

hunches.claim: The target-framework test validates preprocessor text but never compiles the generated output for either an unavailable-attribute target or an available-attribute target, so it does not test the acceptance criterion that generated code still compiles on every supported target framework.

receipt_plan.detail: Run the generator with preprocessor symbols NETSTANDARD2_0 and NETFRAMEWORK, respectively, and assert successful compilation against corresponding reference assemblies without ExcludeFromCodeCoverage; also compile without those symbols against a modern reference set. The current ExcludeAttributeIsGuardedForTargetsWhereItIsUnavailable test would not detect compilation errors that occur despite the expected guard text.

hunches.claim: The newline fix for constrained nesting types has no regression test: the new test input contains no nested generic type with constraints and does not assert generator compilation diagnostics.

refused.what: Which reading of REQ-2297 is intended (A or B)
refused.why: 3 of 3 independent readers found two readings: A: Decorate every generated type—including formatters, string-key formatters, enum/union formatters, and resolvers—with ExcludeFromCodeCoverage unconditionally and provide no setting; B: Apply ExcludeFromCodeCoverage unconditionally only to generated formatter types, leaving non-formatter generated code such as resolvers without the attribute; the requirement says: 'Ambiguity driver: scope (all generated types vs formatters only) and setting (unconditional vs opt-out) are both open'.

residual_risk: This change touches 238 files (222 generated) in codegen-templates, serializer-format, tests; the highest routed risk is 7/10. 15 file(s) were routed for deep review, 1 for light review and 222 to the regeneration check. The existing source generator tests ran on head: 169 of 169 passed, 0 failed. 9 unverified hunch(es) remain without an executed receipt. It touches risky areas (codegen-templates, serializer-format), so a human must sign off. 4 thing(s) were not checked, including generated formatter bytes (source generator output, base vs head); A/B review branches; tests/MessagePack.Tests and other runtime test suites. By signing off, the signer accepts any defect that only those unchecked paths would have revealed. The change is blocked; signing off is not offered until the blocker is fixed.

interpretations.label: A
interpretations.summary: Decorate every generated type—including formatters, string-key formatters, enum/union formatters, and resolvers—with ExcludeFromCodeCoverage unconditionally and provide no setting. Code: Update all relevant source-generator transforms so every emitted generated type receives the attribute, conditionally emitting it only as needed for target-framework compatibility, and update all affected verified snapshots; unlike the narrower reading, resolver and other non-formatter generated types are included, and unlike the opt-out reading no configuration API is added.

interpretations.label: B
interpretations.summary: Apply ExcludeFromCodeCoverage unconditionally only to generated formatter types, leaving non-formatter generated code such as resolvers without the attribute. Code: Change the formatter-related transforms and their snapshots but not resolver or other generated-type templates; the emitted coverage behavior and scope of modified snapshots differ from the all-generated-types reading.
